content: What is ISO 27001 and why is it important?

ISO/IEC 27001 is the world's leading international standard for information security management systems (ISMS). It provides a framework of policies and procedures that includes all legal, physical and technical controls involved in an organisation's information risk management processes. It is important because it helps organisations systematically examine information security risks, implement a coherent suite of controls, and demonstrate compliance to customers, partners, and regulators. The 2022 revision updates the standard to address modern cyber threats and cloud environments.
What new controls were introduced in the 2022 revision?

The 2022 revision introduced 11 new controls. These include: Threat intelligence (5.7), Information security for use of cloud services (5.23), ICT readiness for business continuity (5.30), Physical security monitoring (7.4), Configuration management (8.9), Information deletion (8.10), Data masking (8.11), Data leakage prevention (8.12), Monitoring activities (8.16), Web filtering (8.23), and Secure coding (8.28). These additions reflect the evolving threat landscape, particularly around cloud computing and data protection.
How does ISO 27001 relate to GDPR compliance?

According to the document, ISO 27001 certification can directly support GDPR compliance in several ways. It demonstrates implementation of appropriate technical and organisational measures as required by Article 32 GDPR, provides evidence of data protection by design and by default (Article 25 GDPR), establishes a systematic approach to breach detection and response aligned with Articles 33–34 GDPR, and supports the accountability principle through documented policies and procedures (Article 5(2) GDPR). While ISO 27001 certification does not automatically confer GDPR compliance, it provides a strong foundation.
